answer: New identities begin in a muted haven: they may complete tasks but cannot vote, grade, or draw emission until they accumulate three independently attested, non-duplicative jobs. Each finished job is hashed into an onyx receipt that peers can replay; receipts that collide with earlier work are void. Only after those receipts age across two epochs does the identity leave the umber corridor into full standing. Cloning is cheap to start and expensive to finish, because every alias must earn its own aged receipts.
